title: Streaming fanout recovery & transient capacity gating playbook
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Summary: During a regional capacity surge on 2025-10-29 we observed a class of streaming outages characterized by abrupt client disconnects, fragmented partial-token deliveries, and long tail latencies for high-fanout requests. Impact: ~18% of streaming sessions in the affected region experienced either incomplete output (partial tokens) or early socket terminations for > 3 minutes. Root cause (hypothesis validated by traces): a cascade where sudden fanout of large requests (many simultaneous streaming subscribers) drove worker queues on the per-shard fanout proxy to saturation. Under saturation, internal backpressure signals were coalesced/lost during a race with socket close handling which led to: 1) partial flushes of the outgoing token buffer, 2) incorrect KV cache reconciliation on reconnect, and 3) transient token duplication in a small percentage of sessions. Observability gaps: insufficient per-request fanout depth histograms and no direct counter for "backpressure-signal-dropped" at the proxy layer. This ticket captures immediate postmortem follow-ups and a hardened playbook to reduce both recurrence and customer-visible impact.
action_items: Add per-request fanout and queue-depth metrics to the fanout proxy (owner: Rahul Desai, due: 2025-11-18)
Introduce a lightweight backpressure-ACK protocol between worker and proxy to avoid signal coalescing (owner: Marcus Green, due: 2025-11-25)
Implement 'graceful-output-drain' on socket close to ensure buffered tokens are flushed or atomically checkpointed (owner: Lena Kovács, due: 2025-12-05)
Short-term capacity gating: when fanout depth > threshold, switch new sessions to degraded-mode (no live streaming, buffered polling) and record metrics (owner: Rahul Desai, due: 2025-11-20)
Add KV-cache reconciliation test harness and a canary for reconnect token continuity (owner: QA Team / test infra, due: 2025-12-10)
Post-implementation chaos test to reproduce fanout storms (owner: Reliability Eng, due: 2026-01-15)
comments: 2025-11-08 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after incident retro. Attached initial trace slices and incident timeline in links below.

2025-11-10 - Rahul Desai: Root-cause triage complete. Reproduced queue saturation locally with a scripted fanout generator. Observed backpressure ACK drops when queue-length sampling aligns with socket-close handler.

2025-11-12 - Lena Kovács: Design proposal for 'graceful-output-drain' uploaded to Confluence: includes lightweight token-commit handshake and bounded drain timeout. Requesting review from runtime team.
2025-11-14 - Marcus Green: Prototype for backpressure-ACK added. Early results show eliminated ACK coalescing in synthetic tests. Need PR for integration with proxy message loop.
2025-11-16 - Rahul Desai: Rolled out short-term capacity gating to staging. Observed correct routing to buffered polling for large fanouts. Will schedule a small prod canary on 2025-11-20.
2025-11-18 - QA: KV-cache reconciliation harness accepts reconnect scenarios; found an edge-case for partial bytes where commit id was empty string — added a test and created ENG-61338 to address.
2025-11-19 - Marcus Green: Draft PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4871. Includes backpressure ACK and proxy metrics. Requesting design review from Ava and Rahul.
2025-11-20 - Ava Martinez: Approved PR after small refactor. Rahul to coordinate staged rollout with on-call and runbook updates. Moving ticket to In Progress for implementation tracking.
notes: Trade-offs considered: full request admission control (reject new streams) vs degraded polling fallback. Chose degraded polling for better customer experience while we iterate on throughput controls. Longer-term: consider backpressure-aware scheduler in runtime to avoid proxy queues entirely.
